concept.name: Time and sales
concept.definition: A real-time, trade-by-trade record of executions in an instrument, showing for each trade its time, price, and volume (and typically direction relative to the bid/ask). It is the modern digital descendant of the ticker tape and the raw feed from which footprint and delta statistics are built.
concept.intuition: Time and sales is the market's transaction ledger: every fill, in sequence, with its size and price.
concept.mechanics: Exchanges disseminate each executed trade in market-data feeds; platforms render it as a scrolling table, often color-coded by whether the trade occurred at, inside, or outside the bid/ask, with filters by size or price to isolate large prints.
concept.failure_modes: The raw stream is extremely fast in liquid markets and includes block reports, spreads, and auction prints that distort the apparent flow; aggregated feeds bundle multiple executions into one print, hiding sequence.
concept.misconceptions: Watching the tape does not reveal 'who' is trading — it shows anonymous executions; attribution to institutions or intent is inference, not data.
concept.example: A T&S window shows 100 XYZ at $65.84 at 12:31:54, upticked and colored at the ask, followed by three 2,500-share prints at the same price — the trader notes unusual size hitting the offer.

citations.source: Investopedia — Understanding Time and Sales for Advanced Trading Strategies
